title: U.S. House · Missouri's 4th District
area: West-central and mid-Missouri, including Columbia's outskirts, Raymore, Lebanon and rural counties stretching toward the Lake of the Ozarks.

context.text: The 4th District attracted the most candidates of any Missouri U.S. House race in 2026: ten total, including incumbent Mark Alford, two other Republicans and seven Democrats. Alford won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over Heather Shelton and Scott Vera. Jordan Herrera won a seven-way Democratic primary. Thomas Holbrook advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary. KathleenMae Rogers is running as a write-in, no-party candidate.

candidates.name: Mark Alford

summary.text: Mark Alford is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 4th District. A former television news anchor and real estate professional, he serves on the House Appropriations Committee and chairs the Small Business Committee's Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations Subcommittee.

background.text: Graduated from Baytown Sterling High School in 1982.
Career experience includes working as a team lead and realtor with ReeceNichols Real Estate and as a team lead manager with VortexKC/Chartwell, prior to a career as a television news anchor.

priorities.text: Official House issues page organizes his stated priorities around agriculture, national security, the Second Amendment, small businesses and veterans.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), including the Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies subcommittee and the Military Construction, Veterans Affairs and Related Agencies subcommittee (Vice Chair).
Chairs the Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations Subcommittee of the House Committee on Small Business in the 119th Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Alford has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026, and his official issues page listed only topic headings without body text in this pass. Key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Jordan Herrera
candidates.ballotNote: Won a seven-candidate August 4, 2026 Democratic primary

summary.text: Jordan Herrera is the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 4th District. A nearly 16-year U.S. Air Force veteran who later served as a Missouri Assistant Attorney General, he is campaigning on lowering costs, healthcare, veterans' issues and national security.

background.text: Born in Scottsbluff, Nebraska; served in the U.S. Air Force from 2006 to 2022, receiving multiple Air Force awards; graduated from Sidney High School.
Earned an associate degree from Air University (2008), a bachelor's degree from Park University (2020), and a law degree from Southwestern Law School-Los Angeles (2024).
Served as an Assistant Attorney General for the State of Missouri after leaving the Air Force.

priorities.text: Economic security: lowering everyday costs, expanding access to affordable housing, protecting healthcare and raising wages to keep up with cost of living.
National defense: says national security requires a modern, ready military that uses taxpayer dollars responsibly while supporting service members and veterans.
Freedom and privacy: says government should protect individual rights and personal privacy.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
